basis: Re-derived independently, no DB contact. (a) Object exists: internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/000001_initial_schema.up.sql:514 CREATE TABLE marketmovers_config, under the '-- Market Movers integration' banner at :510-512. (b) RLS granted: 000003_supabase_security_and_perf_fixes.up.sql:169-170 (ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + 'service role bypass' policy). (c) Sibling claim verified by reading 000021_drop_market_movers.up.sql in full: it drops idx_mm_sales_comps_lookup, mm_sales_comps, mm_card_mappings, idx_purchases_mm_last_error, and seven mm_* columns on campaign_purchases. marketmovers_config is genuinely absent from that list. (d) Repo-wide, not Go-only: 'git grep -nE "\bmarketmovers_config\b" -- $(git ls-files)' returns hits ONLY in the two migrations above (plus 000001 down.sql:33 and 000003 down.sql:131-132), docs/SCHEMA.md:852,995, and audit/plan/spec files. Zero hits in internal/, cmd/, web/, scripts/. (e) LENS-BRIEF §3 trap 3 (stale sqlite. comment) does not carry the finding: deadness here rests on the migration history and the repo-wide reference count, not on the ':513 -- marketmovers_config: sqlite.MarketMoversConfig' comment. Independently checked the four sibling stale-comment tables: cardladder_config (cardladder_store.go, 6 matches), cl_card_mappings (8 files), scheduler_run_stats (2 files) are all live; mm_card_mappings has zero Go refs AND was dropped by 000021 — so the comment form is not predictive either way, consistent with the finding. (f) Dependent-object check: grepping ALL 50 migration files (up+down) for the table name yields only the four locations in (d) — no view, no FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES marketmovers_config, no trigger, no index. Nothing depends on it. (g) Hidden-reference check 9 (string-built SQL): 'git grep -nE "\bMarketMovers[A-Za-z]*\b" -- "*.go"' returns nothing (exit 1), and I read every fmt.Sprintf-built query in internal/adapters/storage/postgres/ (integration_failures.go:71,106,127; pricing_store.go:131; purchase_dh_query_store.go:97,120) — all interpolate column names or WHERE-clause predicates only, never a table name. No dynamic path can reach this table. All five of the finding's evidence commands execute and their substance reproduces.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Two defects, neither fatal to the central claim. (1) EVIDENCE TRANSCRIPTION, item 5: the recorded output for 'git grep -cE ...' is wrong in shape and in one value. git grep -c prints 'file:count' per file; the finding recorded bare integers that are file counts, and for cardladder_config it recorded '1' when the real output is 'internal/adapters/storage/postgres/cardladder_store.go:6' (one file, six matches). The command still runs and every table is still non-zero, so the conclusion drawn from it survives; the transcription does not. (2) IRREVERSIBILITY — the material gap. I agree with the controller's expectation: static analysis establishes that the schema OBJECT is dead, but it cannot establish that no production data of value lives in it, and that sub-question is unresolvable by this audit's method. The acceptance_criteria as written are unsafe for an irreversible operation: the proposed .down.sql recreates the table STRUCTURE only, so rollback does not restore rows, yet no criterion tells the fixer to check the live row count first. The ticket must add a precondition: 'SELECT count(*) FROM marketmovers_config returns 0 (or its contents are reviewed and explicitly discarded) before the DROP is authored.' Separately, the finding under-describes what is in the table: it holds username and encrypted_refresh_token (000001:516-517) for a retired vendor. That is a mild argument FOR dropping it (a stale credential sitting in production) rather than against, and does not raise the severity — 'low' is correct for an inert, undepended-upon table.

basis: Settled entirely from file contents. Creation sites: 'grep -n CREATE TABLE' over both migrations gives 000017_psa_portal_snapshot.up.sql:1 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS psa_portal_snapshot, and 000018_psa_campaign_sync.up.sql:3 psa_campaign_snapshot and :11 psa_campaign_push_queue. Doc sites: docs/SCHEMA.md:568 '### `psa_campaign_snapshot`' whose provenance line is :584 '**Added:** migration 000017', and :588 '### `psa_campaign_push_queue`' whose provenance line is :613, same text. I confirmed by reading :566-590 that :584 falls inside the snapshot section and precedes the push_queue header, so the citations belong to the sections the finding assigns them to. Checked the controller's 'misleading vs wrong' fork directly: 'git grep -nE psa_campaign -- internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/000017*' returns nothing (exit 1), and I read 000017_psa_portal_snapshot.up.sql in full — it is a single CREATE TABLE for the unrelated singleton psa_portal_snapshot and does not create, alter, index, or otherwise touch either psa_campaign table. So the doc is flatly WRONG, not merely misleading, and the finding's one-token fix (000017 -> 000018 in both places) is the correct one. Both of the finding's doc-quoting evidence commands reproduce, though the first only via its '||' fallback: the pattern 'Added: migration' does not match the file, whose literal text is '**Added:** migration 000017'; the sed fallback then prints the expected line, so the command exits 0 with the recorded output.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Nothing material. One cosmetic note for the fixer's acceptance criteria: the second criterion, "grep -n 'Added: migration 000017' docs/SCHEMA.md no longer matches either section", is vacuously satisfiable — that literal pattern already matches nothing today, because the file's text is '**Added:** migration 000017' with bold markers. The criterion should be written against the real text (e.g. `grep -n '\*\*Added:\*\* migration 000017' docs/SCHEMA.md`) so it can actually fail before the fix and pass after. This does not affect the verdict; the defect and the fix are both correct as stated.
